A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GSSBO and retain the same research objective and core experiments. The main texts, equations, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-function and diabetes NAS experiments, runtime measurements, sample-distribution analysis, and posterior-mean RMSE results.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark and NAS results, with additional comparator and surrogate-model experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 introduces a one-time 'switched' flag that fixes the buffer after the timing threshold is crossed; v1 could reset its size after subsequent slow iterations. The gradient-selection criterion and retention of initial/latest observations remain. Appendix B.5 also introduces deep-kernel and BNN surrogate variants.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Eggholder2, Hart6, Levy20, Powell50, Rastrigin100, and the UCI diabetes NAS task. The added comparisons reuse these problems, including Hart6 for the alternative-surrogate experiments.

E2.justification: The main comparisons add IPA and mini-META. Appendix B.3–B.4 adds K-means++, REMBO, and HESBO, spelled HSEBO in Figure 9. The sparse baseline is also reported differently: SVIGP citing Hensman et al. in v1 becomes SparseGP citing Lawrence et al. in v2.

E3.justification: The main experimental budget increases from 400 to 1,000 iterations, reflected in Figures 2–4. Added appendix comparisons have plots extending to approximately 400 iterations and include deep-kernel/BNN configurations. Newly specified NAS ranges and initial sample counts are disclosures rather than established changes to retained settings.

E4.justification: v1's posterior-mean RMSE validation using 10,000 test samples is removed. v2 adds Hart6 checks of selection with deep-kernel and BNN surrogates. The existing Z sensitivity analysis remains, and the sample-distribution study moves from Section 6.3 to Appendix B.2 without changing its graphic.

E5.justification: Both specify 50 repetitions per experiment and five repetitions per NAS evaluation. Shaded variability reporting continues without newly specified seed identities, interval definitions, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v2 supplies revised main result curves and additional comparator and surrogate results, while removing the posterior-RMSE curve. Section 6.1 reports roughly half the GP-UCB runtime at 400 iterations in v1 versus roughly 10% at 1,000 iterations in v2; these are different-budget results, not a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Theorem 5.2 and Appendix A substantially revise the confidence parameter and penalty/regret derivations to include the variance-error term B. v2 adds claimed equivalence to greedy Nyström selection, a gradient-versus-random approximation analysis, and a 5% kernel-error criterion for minimum subset size. v1's Woodbury derivation is removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims: gradient-selected subsets accelerate BO while preserving competitive optimization performance and GP-UCB-like sublinear regret. The added experiments and derivations do not materially redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations contrasting GSSBO with SparseGP correction terms and attributing REMBO/HESBO weaknesses to lost dimensional information. Appendix B.5 distinguishes GP-specific theory from broader surrogate applicability. The RMSE-based accuracy interpretation and conservative-penalty caveat are removed, while the over-exploitation explanation is retained in Appendix B.2.

D1.justification: v2 adds Apple M2 Pro hardware specifications, 20 initial samples, a typical buffer size near 100, and explicit NAS hyperparameter ranges where v1 only described a normalized four-dimensional space. The perturbation variance of 0.01 and maximum-likelihood kernel fitting were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands positioning against scalable BO, gradient-informed models, and RKHS/Nyström selection, including IPA, mini-META, Ash et al., Oglic, and Hayakawa. Corresponding references and substantive comparisons are added, while the Wei et al. FASS discussion and reference disappear.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, and gradient explanations receive localized rewrites and expansions. Background becomes Preliminaries, the distribution study moves to the appendix, and citation style changes. Most section ordering and substantial portions of the narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes a single-column preprint with substantially different author, figure, and page layouts. Existing illustrations are relocated, main plots receive longer axes and expanded legends, the RMSE figure disappears, and new appendix comparison figures are added.

improvement.justification: v2 broadens empirical comparisons, documents useful settings, and includes the previously omitted variance-error contribution in its penalty construction. However, it removes direct posterior-RMSE validation and adds a Nyström-equivalence argument that incorrectly treats invertibility of K inverse as sufficient to preserve norm rankings (Appendix A.1). These empirical and documentation gains coexist with substantive theoretical reliability concerns, leaving the net quality change unclear.
